api: Not a general-purpose API product. Extensibility is through editor extensions and GitHub.
cons: Behind dedicated agentic editors on large refactors
Premium request caps can surprise heavy users
Quality varies by language and by editor
name: GitHub Copilot
files: Works against the open repository and editor context. Repository-wide awareness varies by tier and editor.
value: The safest institutional choice for AI-assisted coding: broad IDE support, mature enterprise administration, and an established procurement path. Rarely the most capable option, usually the easiest to approve.
engine: Multiple underlying models, primarily OpenAI, with other model options in some tiers.
latency: Low latency for completion, which is the property that matters most for inline use.

pricing.includes: Policy controls, audit logs, IP indemnity

quality: Strong at idiomatic completion and boilerplate. Weaker at large multi-file refactors, where dedicated agentic tools have moved ahead.
tagline: The most widely deployed AI coding assistant, and the default in most enterprises.
use_cases: Inline code completion across the editors teams already use
Explaining unfamiliar code and assisting review
integrations: VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains IDEs, Neovim
governance_note: The enterprise tiers carry IP indemnity for suggestions, which is usually the deciding factor for legal review rather than any capability difference.
training_optout: Business and enterprise tiers exclude customer code from model training. A public-code filter is available. Confirm current terms for your tier.
